brief: The thirtieth statue holding a long unrolled scroll that trails behind her; Śuka reading it aloud with a raised wing; Dādī smiling; Lubdhaka's foreman following the words with his finger.

The eighth statue with her lips slightly parted as if hissing, a faint curl of breath; Śuka counting on his claws; Dādī pointing at three inscribed words on a pillar; Lubdhaka's foreman holding his lamp higher.

The temple library at night: Dhūmaka, now silver and glowing, rises from the desk in a spiral like smoke from a lamp just put out, smiling and waving; the half-burnt leaf blazes gold with its first line lit; you (seen from behind), Dādī and Śuka look up in wonder.

Early morning in the temple library: Śuka the parrot at an open window with the sunrise behind him, beak wide open mid-squawk, wings half spread; Dādī at the reading desk lowering her round spectacles with one eyebrow raised, amused; Dhūmaka giggling as a little puff of smoke beside the glowing leaf.
